slides.texte_overlay:
How To Master The Art
Of Small Talk
Have a go-to question for every setting. At work: "What are you working on?" At a party: "How do you know the host?" A ready question removes the panic.
Turn closed questions into open ones. Not "Did you have a good weekend?" but "What was the best part of your weekend?" One word changes the whole chat.
Share a tiny opinion. "I think autumn is the best season, change my mind." A light opinion gives people something fun to react to.
Notice what's happening around you. The music, the view, the food. Comments about the moment feel natural and never forced.
Keep your head full of fresh topics. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and small talk is easy when you always have something new.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Small talk is easy when you always have something new.

slides.texte_overlay: Give people an easy exit. "I'll let you get back to your friends." Ending kindly and warmly makes people happy to talk to you again the next time you meet.
Practise every day in small ways. The cashier, the neighbour, the colleague in the lift. Daily reps turn small talk from something you dread into something you actually enjoy.
